speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities in more detail, such as whether it is raised, flat, or blistered? Also, how many days ago did these symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash appear as flat, red, blotchy macules that give a "slapped cheek" appearance on the face, followed by a lacy, reticular pattern on the body? Have you noticed any joint pain or swelling in her hands, wrists, or knees?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, followed by a lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities, is classic for Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
